scenes.headline: How Ideogram Vector turns a picture into shapes
scenes.sub: Forty sample SVG files, opened and measured
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Kerning! Ideogram's new model makes SVG files. There is no paper, so I opened its sample files.

scenes.text: The files read like a raster traced into filled outlines, where any shape whose colour ramps gets its own fitted gradient instead of a stack of flat bands.
scenes.say: The files read like a picture traced into outlines, with a fitted gradient wherever the colour ramps.

steps.say: Probably, a prompt first becomes a picture. Every gallery file shares one square canvas.
Each colour region is traced and fitted with curves. Path starts land on a quarter pixel grid, a tracer's mark.
A region whose colour ramps gets a gradient of its own.
Out comes a flat list of filled paths, in the same format the image vectorizer writes.

scenes.title: Inside one file

items.say: There is no text element anywhere. Every letter is a filled outline.
No groups, no strokes, just shapes back to front.
A letter's hole is a dark blob painted on top.

scenes.say: Here is what a single file holds.

left.title: VTracer
left.say: A classical tracer like VTracer has only flat colours, so a smooth ramp becomes a staircase of bands.

right.title: Ideogram Vector
right.say: Ideogram fits a gradient to each ramp, and draws the same lettering in a fraction of the shapes.

steps.say: In Ideogram's SVG the letters fade smoothly from cyan to lavender, like the source.
VTracer's flat layers band the same ramp and leave an outline around each letter.

scenes.title: PSNR against the Starlight source
scenes.say: On that lettering, Ideogram's small file matches the source far more closely.

scenes.text: Filled outlines with fitted gradients: vectors that scale and stay small, not type you can retype.
scenes.say: So think of it as filled outlines with fitted gradients. They scale and stay small, but the type is a drawing of type.
Letters are outlines. Each ramp gets its own gradient. And it shares a writer with the vectorizer.
